This stuff does exactly as described!. So far, I absolutely LOVE this soap! I ordered the sampler pack. I started with the Pine Tar, because I thought it would be my least favorite, as I'm not a huge fan of "pine" scented products. However, I was surprised! The smell is very strong at first, and remains pretty strong when it sits in the shower. However, it is much more subtle on your skin. it leaves my skin pretty soft (which was a shock,) and I felt cleaner than I had with Irish Spring, which I'd been using for years. It surprised me again when it removed the remaining grease from my skin left behind by the Gojo I use after working on my projects.
That's not to say it works miracles, because it doesn't. It does exactly as the manufacturer describes!
This isn't Lava Soap, Fast Orange, or some other heavy duty hand cleaner. It's an all natural, GREAT smelling bar of soap. If you need something stronger, better buy IT first.
I've seen some reviewers complain about how long it lasts, claiming only 3 days. The photo I posted is after 30 days of use. Yes, 1 month. Now, I'm not a huge guy. 5'6", 150 lbs, average build. Very good clone, moderate longevity. Grand Parfums Versace Eros opens with a strong projection of citrus, fruity, sweet, musky and spicy notes. The opening is very fresh, sharp, bright, inviting, unique, and delectable. The green apple, mint, ambroxan, and lemon are the most prominent opening notes. The lemon is the fresh and bright opening note, astringent, sour, and vibrant; the green apple is by its side, delectable, sweet, sour, crispy, and acidic. The mint rounds up the opening with its cooling green and slightly spicy note. The ambroxan is also noticeable musky, lemony, and ambery note that works well, improving the fragrance's projection. As the fragrance moves towards its dry down, the tonka bean and vanilla add a sweet and aromatic touch without making the fragrance overly sweet or taking the focus away from the mint, green apple, and lemon. The vetiver, oakmoss, and cedar are part of the support notes; they combine their notes to create a fresh green and woody accord but remain in the back of the fragrance. The fragrance is linear, all notes come up as soon as the fragrance is applied and continue into the dry down. Once Grand Parfums Versace Eros has reached its full dry down, it can be summarized as a strong projection, spicy mint, fruity green apple, musky ambroxan, mildly sweet vanilla, tonka, and woody cedar fragrance. The fragrance feels casual, comforting, delectable, energizing, exquisite, fresh, fruity, green, high-quality, inviting, masculine, modern, musky, nicely-blended, playful, refreshing, rich, sharp, seductive, sour, sparkly, special, sweet, unique, versatile, wild, woody, and very pleasant.

DISLIKE RATING: 0/10. The fragrance contains no offensive or harsh notes.

French Soap: It will Forever Change Your Definition of the Word "Soap". About twenty years ago, I made my first trip to France. Since we were there for a few weeks, I had to purchase some bar soap, and picked up, at random, some Provencal soap at our local supermarket (soap is soap, right? who cares what brand it is?).

When I first used it, the shock I experienced was something that made me realize that the soap I had been using all my life wasn't really "soap," at all, but was rather a chemical concoction. Of course, it works. It's just that when I tried my first bar of milled soap from the Provence in France I immediately could see all the differences: the silky smooth lather, the smell that was real, not chemical; the cleaning power; the feeling after drying off. An absolutely different experience.

Since that time, my wife and I regularly bring back as much real Provencal soap as we can when we visit France. It's actually not that expensive in France, at least for the standard brands. But the difficulty is the weight: putting all this soap in your suitcase pushes against airline luggage weight limits, and it has become a standard challenge we deal with each trip. But that how much we like this REAL soap.

Now, here's the thing. You can go to shops in the United States, and find soaps that say "Made in France," and so you just believe it. Do a little digging, however, and you'll find that there are companies that market soap in the US with the words "Made in France" emboldened across the front are not actually selling something made in France: it's that they are getting one small component of their blend from France, and then manufacture it here very much like any other US soap is made. I feel this is fraudulent, yet it is such an arcance subject that no one cares to look into it. But anyone who has tried the real thing knows the difference.

Snozzle with Xtava Black Orchid and Conair Infinity Pro. Similar to some of the other reviewers experiences, I find that the SnozzlePro works pretty well for me, but I do have to be very careful and make frequent adjustments -- it sort of exploits design problems with the tools you are using. I used it with a Conair Infinity ProPro and an Xtava Black Orchid.

Pros:
-It definitely fits my Conair Infinity Pro and probably won't have any trouble fitting other hair dryers.
-It's thick enough to be sturdy, but thin enough that I can stretch it onto the hair dryer.
- I don't experience any leaking or weird smells.
-I can use it (carefully) with the Xtava.

Cons:
-It is made of rubber, so when it heats up the rubber becomes more pliable and loose around the diffuser. I would recommend using this with cold air if possible. Unfortunately, my Conair Infinity Pro has a setting for "Cool" that isn't cold enough. So, I find that this works best if I keep my finger on the blue "Cold Shot" button the whole time.
-The Xtava has a very short connection point, so even though the SnozzlePro works pretty well, there's not a ton of space for it to hold on. That's a problem with the Xtava though, not the SnozzlePro. In particular, it seems to detach most at the top of the connection point and it will fall off while I'm using it. I just sort of use it gently and keep an eye on that top part to make sure it isn't slipping out.

Overall, I think the SnozzlePro is a great product that would probably work best with a diffuser with a longer connection point than the Xtava and potentially a hair dryer that has a truly cold setting.
